title: Acme Corp - POC timeline & milestones
next_steps: Redwood to send POC statement of work and pilot plan by 2025-04-11
Customer to provide test dataset + example prompts (anonymized) by 2025-04-14
Schedule kickoff & access setup call for week of 2025-04-14
Redwood to run baseline latency/throughput benchmarks (hosted + dedicated) within first week of access
Schedule mid-point review (week 3) and exec readout (week 6) tentative dates to be confirmed
action_items: Evan Miller - Draft and share SOW/pilot plan - due 2025-04-11
Jordan Lee - Share anonymized test dataset and 10 representative prompt templates - due 2025-04-14
Maya Singh - Prepare benchmark checklist and infra access steps (SSH keys, VPC peering docs) - due 2025-04-13
Noah Rivera - Provision test VPC endpoint and KMS policy with read-only logs access - due 2025-04-15
Lina Gomez - Provide success criteria and exec slide template for readout - due 2025-04-17
transcript: 00:00 Evan Miller: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time today. This is Evan from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Maya, our solutions engineer. 00:08 Maya Singh: Hi all, Maya here. We'll focus on the POC timeline, milestone cadence, benchmarks we plan to run, and what access we need. 00:16 Priya Patel: Great, thanks. We're mostly focused on getting a reproducible benchmark and an exec readout at the end. 00:22 Jordan Lee: Quick context, our primary workload is customer-facing summarization and a search re-ranker. Avg prompt size about 120 tokens, responses ~200 tokens, peak concurrency around 60 qps during business hours, baseline p99 latency target under 250ms. 00:39 Maya Singh: Helpful. For sizing we typically ask for: QPS profile (avg/peak), token length distribution, and any long-tail prompts. For the POC we'll run both latency-sensitive and throughput runs. 00:50 Noah Rivera: Security wise we need SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML setup, and KMS/HSM integration for any key material. Also if you support VPC peering that's preferred — we can't send raw data off-network. 01:04 Evan Miller: Yes, we can do a Private deployment option for VPC with a customer-managed control plane, we also support dedicated pools if you want predictable throughput. We'll send SOC2 + ISO docs and a short security checklist. 01:16 Priya Patel: Cool. For success criteria, the exec team will want: p99 latency <200ms for the summarization path or a clear mitigation plan, average cost per 100k tokens below our target (we'll supply target $/100k), and quality A/B vs current model showing no regression on our evaluation set. 01:33 Lina Gomez: We'll quantify quality as Pass/Fail on 4 key metrics: factuality, relevance, hallucination rate, response length compliance. 01:42 Maya Singh: Sounds good. Proposed milestones: Kickoff + access setup (week 0), baseline benchmarks (days 2-7), mid-point review (week 3) to show interim results and tune batching/quantization, then an exec readout at week 6 with final benchmarks and runbook. 01:58 Jordan Lee: That timeline seems reasonable. Do you plan to run both Hosted API and Dedicated setups? 02:04 Evan Miller: We can run both. Typical approach: start with hosted Redwood API for quick latency baselines, then spin up a Dedicated pool (or Private if you require VPC) to measure steady-state throughput and cost. We'll compare p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost estimates. 02:20 Priya Patel: Benchmarks — what exact tests will you run? 02:24 Maya Singh: We'll run synthetic load with your prompt templates to capture tail latency, a representative L0 throughput test with warm KV cache, and a cold-cache run to emulate first-time queries. We'll also run quality evals using your labeled set (we'll only use anonymized examples). 02:40 Maya Singh: Metrics we collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, batch sizes, and per-token cost. We'll export results into a shared spreadsheet. 02:51 Jordan Lee: For hardware, if we go dedicated, what GPU class do you recommend? 02:55 Maya Singh: For the model family you described (70B-ish or quantized variants), we usually recommend an A100 or equivalent with quantization to int8/4 where possible; if you want lower latency, smaller sharded replicas with NVLink can help. We'll propose config options in the SOW. 03:12 Noah Rivera: A note about networking — we'll need clear steps to set up VPC peering and test endpoints. We prefer peering + private endpoints rather than exposing keys over internet. 03:21 Evan Miller: Understood. We'll include a detailed access checklist: IP ranges, firewall rules, KMS roles, service account setup, and a sample cURL for the test harness. 03:33 Lina Gomez: Who owns the mid-point review? We want someone technical who can explain tuning decisions. 03:38 Maya Singh: Maya will run the mid-point demo and Evan will join for product/contract questions. The mid-point will include tuning actions: batching changes, KV cache strategies, and potential quantization adjustments. 03:51 Priya Patel: On the quality side, if your model shows higher hallucination we need an action plan — either prompt engineering, reranker, or fallback to smaller model. 03:58 Evan Miller: Agreed. Our rollouts support canarying between model variants and automatic fallback to a more conservative model if quality drops. We'll capture that in the runbook. 04:08 Jordan Lee: Can you share an example of a previous POC timeline? 04:12 Evan Miller: Sure — typical POC: Week 0 kickoff & access, Days 1-7 baseline runs, Week 2 instrumentation + tuning, Week 3 mid-point review, Week 4-5 follow-ups and longer throughput runs, Week 6 exec readout. We can compress or expand depending on availability. 04:30 Maya Singh: On benchmarks we'll also include reproducibility notes: seed settings, dataset splits, and exact versions of model checkpoints and quantization recipes. 04:40 Priya Patel: About costs — we need a ballpark for the Dedicated option for planning. 04:44 Evan Miller: We'll include cost estimates in the SOW. Roughly, dedicated pools have a fixed hourly/throughput cost plus per-token runtime cost; we'll model it against your expected qps and monthly request volume. 04:56 Jordan Lee: Who will set up the benchmark harness? 04:59 Maya Singh: Redwood will provide a harness (docker image + simple client), but we ask you to run it initially in your environment to validate network and keys. We can also run a cloud-based harness if you prefer. 05:10 Noah Rivera: We'll do the harness inside our VPC. We'll need a short guide. 05:13 Evan Miller: We'll deliver that. 05:16 Lina Gomez: Regarding deliverables at exec readout — we expect a one-page summary, performance graphs, cost model, quality evaluation, and recommended next steps. 05:25 Maya Singh: We'll prepare a slide deck template for the readout and a short runbook showing how to go from POC to production. 05:33 Jordan Lee: Any risks you foresee? 05:35 Maya Singh: Main risks are: dataset mismatch causing quality variance, network limitations affecting p99 latency, and unexpected token distributions causing higher cost. Mitigations: define representative prompt set, run cold/warm cache tests, and tune batching/quantization. 05:49 Priya Patel: Ok let's lock dates tentatively: Kickoff next Wednesday 2025-04-16, mid-point review 2025-05-07, exec readout 2025-05-28. Are those doable? 05:59 Evan Miller: Tentatively yes, subject to access being provisioned by 2025-04-15. We'll put those dates in the SOW and adjust as needed. 06:08 Jordan Lee: One more question — will you run an A/B vs our current provider? 06:12 Maya Singh: Yes we can run A/B tests against an external API as long as labels and evaluation scripts are shared. We'll record paired comparisons for quality and latency. 06:22 Priya Patel: Great. Recap and next steps please. 06:25 Evan Miller: Recap: Evan to send SOW/pilot plan by 4/11; Maya will prepare benchmark checklist and harness; customer to share anonymized dataset and prompt templates by 4/14; access & VPC peering to be set up by 4/15; baseline runs in days 1-7 after access; mid-point review week 3 (5/7); exec readout week 6 (5/28). Action items noted in the chat. 06:47 Lina Gomez: Sounds good. We'll look for the SOW. Thanks everyone. 06:50 Evan Miller: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to security docs and a shared spreadsheet for benchmarks. 06:54 End of recording.
